{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-or-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"b89155c6f3fe218199700488950ac20b1acbd2d5d6fc020034b1a8927b29ec45","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-or-class-c:lineage:14","source_registry_sha256":"ce8335c1d96ff7ed209bf236ba9a56fe92dfebd915bc0e2fa7fb830ee03f0f09","source_liveness_sha256":"c4da479589e7933e4eef7366086dfcc48a420303d0089cb0ea19ad9137abec1d"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Lane travel: curves, lane changes, passing, freeways and towing","heading":"C — Lane travel part two: scanning, curves, changing lanes, passing and no-passing rules, freeway entry and exit, ramp meters, large vehicles and towing","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Lane travel part two: scanning, curves, changing lanes, passing and no-passing rules, freeway entry and exit, ramp meters, large vehicles and towing
Knowledge domain: looking ahead, taking curves, changing lanes and passing safely, where passing is banned, how to enter, drive and leave a freeway, and the extra rules for large vehicles and trailers.

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
Scan for trouble spots as far ahead as you can see, so you rarely need a last-minute move. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
Scanning means taking in the whole scene, roadsides included, so you notice pedestrians, hazards, vehicles that may cut into your path and signs routing you elsewhere. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
Signs that a driver ahead may slow or stop include a cyclist or pedestrian on the road ahead, brake lights coming on and blinking turn signals. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
Slow down before entering a curve, using any speed posted under the curve sign as your guide. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A01
In a curve, look through it to your path, check where oncoming vehicles are in their lane, keep right of the center line in the middle of your lane, and expect hidden cyclists, pedestrians or slow vehicles. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A01
Speed up gradually as you leave a curve. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A01
A blind spot is the area around a vehicle the driver cannot see from the seat even using mirrors, so avoid staying in another driver's blind spot. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A01
Before changing lanes, signal, check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic coming from behind, and glance over the shoulder on the side you are moving toward. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A02
Passing is routine but dangerous, so keep a good view ahead by not tailgating, especially trucks and trailers, and know how fast your vehicle can accelerate. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A02
Pass only with enough room: cutting back too early risks sideswiping the passed vehicle, returning too late risks a head-on crash, and when unsure you stay in your lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A02
On a two-lane road you pass only on the left, starting no sooner than the beginning of a passing zone and finishing before any no-passing zone. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A02
You may not exceed the speed limit to pass, because going over the limit is illegal at all times. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A02
To pass, confirm a clear path, check mirrors and glance over your shoulder toward the new lane, signal, speed up and finish quickly, then signal and return once the passed vehicle shows in your rearview mirror. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A03
Signs and pavement markings show where passing is allowed, and you must never pass where your view of oncoming traffic is limited. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A03
Do not cross the center line to pass inside a no-passing zone, and do not start a pass you cannot finish before reaching one. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A03
Do not pass when a hill or curve blocks your view of oncoming traffic. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A03
Do not pass when approaching, at or inside an intersection or a railroad crossing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A03
Do not pass a vehicle that has stopped at a crosswalk to let a pedestrian cross. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A03
In a no-passing zone you may cross the center line only when the right side of the road is blocked or when you are turning left. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A04
You may pass on the right when the vehicle ahead is turning or signaling left, if there is room without leaving the pavement or using a bike lane and the road ahead of it is clear. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A04
You may also pass on the right on a road with two or more lanes in your direction when the vehicle you pass is in the left lane. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A04
Take extra care when passing on the right, since other drivers do not expect it, and never speed past the limit to do it. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A04
When someone passes you, stay to the right, watch oncoming traffic and adjust your speed so the passer can get back into the right lane quickly. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A04
Never wave or use lights to tell other drivers when to pass; the law forbids flashing any of your signals for that purpose. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-F25 | anchor: A05
Freeways have several lanes each way and higher speeds, and traffic flows better because access is controlled, sharp curves are few and there are no railroad crossings or traffic signals. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-F26 | anchor: A05
Holding a steady speed on a freeway reduces lane changes, while weaving through traffic raises crash risk and rarely saves time. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-F27 | anchor: A05
Keep pace with traffic but do not exceed the posted speed to match the flow, and if you drive slower than the flow, use the right lane. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-F28 | anchor: A05
Watch for vehicles entering the freeway and adjust your speed so they can merge smoothly. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-F29 | anchor: A05
If you see freeway traffic slowing ahead, tap your brake pedal lightly several times to warn the drivers behind you. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-F30 | anchor: A05
Unlike entering most busy roads, you enter a freeway by using the on-ramp to speed up and merge with fast traffic. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-F31 | anchor: A05
When merging onto a freeway, yield to traffic already on it, check mirrors and blind spots, match its speed and keep moving, since drivers behind expect you to accelerate. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-F32 | anchor: A05
If a DO NOT ENTER or WRONG WAY sign shows you are entering a freeway the wrong way, pull to the side of the ramp at once, stop, turn on hazard lights, and carefully turn around or back off the ramp. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-F33 | anchor: A06
Ramp meters look like traffic signals and run only at certain times; on multi-lane ramps each lane has one, only one vehicle goes per green, and you speed up to merge when yours turns green. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-F34 | anchor: A06
A dark ramp meter is not in use, so do not stop at it. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-F35 | anchor: A06
To leave a freeway, signal well ahead, keep your speed until you are off the freeway, then slow to the posted advisory speed on the exit ramp. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-F36 | anchor: A06
Most exits are numbered; if you miss yours, continue to the next one, because you must never stop or back up on a freeway and the shoulder is for emergencies only. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-F37 | anchor: A06
With vehicle trouble on a freeway, move to the right shoulder or an emergency stopping area, turn on hazard lights, and if possible stay in or near the vehicle on the side away from traffic, since walking there is dangerous. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-F38 | anchor: A06
Large vehicles and vehicles towing trailers are longer, higher and wider, take longer to speed up and stop, and need more room to turn. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-F39 | anchor: A06
Driving a pickup with a camper, a motor home or a trailer, check your speed and the traffic behind often, pull off at the first safe turnout when traffic stacks up, and use the right lane on multi-lane roads. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-F40 | anchor: A07
Letting passengers ride in a trailer is illegal, with three exceptions: a commercial bus trailer, a trailer that is independently steered, and a trailer towed by a fifth-wheel device. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec04-F41 | anchor: A07
A fifth-wheel trailer carrying passengers needs safety glazing in its windows and windowed doors, a sound or visual signal to reach the driver, and a clear exit that opens from inside and outside. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec04-F42 | anchor: A07
Oregon law allows a passenger or recreational vehicle to tow at most one boat, utility trailer or other vehicle, so a second trailer or towed vehicle is not allowed. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0044]

Misconceptions: matching the flow of traffic does not excuse going over the posted speed; a dark ramp meter is not a stop signal; passing on the right is not banned outright but allowed only in the listed cases; waving a driver past is not a courtesy, flashing signals for it is unlawful.
Mnemonics: signal, mirror, shoulder before every lane change; slow into a curve, speed out of it; on-ramp means speed up, off-ramp means slow down after you leave; one green, one car at a ramp meter.
Glossary: blind spot means the area around a vehicle the driver cannot see even with mirrors; passing zone means a stretch where markings allow passing; ramp meter means a signal that releases on-ramp traffic one vehicle at a time; turnout means a roadside pull-off where slow vehicles let traffic pass.
Dynamic facts: ramp meters run only at certain times of day, and the fine amounts printed in the towing box are held as debt in part D until their scope is confirmed.
